description: We are a team of passionate developers, engineers, and creative thinkers united by our interest in space exploration and technology. Our goal is to transform complex space mission concepts into an engaging, interactive, and educational experience. Through creativity, scientific curiosity, technical innovation, and teamwork, we aim to build a game that inspires players to think like mission designers and explore the challenges of space exploration.
summary:
NOVALUX is an interactive educational space mission design and operations game that allows participants to experience the challenges of planning and managing a space mission. Players define scientific objectives, design spacecraft, select instruments and launch vehicles, choose orbital destinations, and evaluate engineering constraints such as mass, power, budget, communications and reliability.

The prototype combines spacecraft engineering, orbital simulation, mission planning and interactive learning activities in one platform. Players can test their designs, respond to operational events and evaluate mission performance through simulation and scoring.

NOVALUX addresses the challenge by making complex space engineering concepts more accessible and engaging. It helps learners understand how scientific goals, spacecraft systems and mission operations must work together to achieve mission success.
details:
Project Details

NOVALUX is an interactive space mission design and operations game that allows users to experience the challenges of planning, building, and managing a space mission. Players begin by selecting a mission objective, such as exploring the Moon, Mars, Earth, or deep space. They then make important mission decisions, including choosing a launch vehicle, selecting an orbit, designing a spacecraft, and equipping it with scientific instruments.

The game evaluates each mission using simplified engineering considerations, including spacecraft mass, power requirements, budget, communication capacity, reliability, and scientific objectives. Players can run mission simulations, respond to challenges and unexpected events, and review their mission performance. This interactive approach helps users understand how different engineering decisions affect the success of a space mission.

The main benefit of NOVALUX is that it makes complex space mission concepts more accessible and engaging. Instead of only reading about spacecraft engineering, users can experiment with different designs, learn from unsuccessful decisions, and improve their missions through hands-on gameplay. It encourages critical thinking, creativity, problem-solving, and an understanding of the teamwork involved in space exploration.

Our intended impact is to inspire students and space enthusiasts to explore STEM subjects and develop an interest in aerospace engineering, physics, and space science. NOVALUX aims to demonstrate that mission planning involves balancing many interconnected factors rather than focusing on just one aspect of a spacecraft.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for interactive 3D visualisation. We also used browser-based technologies for mission simulation, spacecraft interactions, and local data storage. The project was designed to run in a web browser without requiring specialised hardware.

NOVALUX is creative because it combines an interactive 3D space environment with mission planning, spacecraft design, engineering constraints, and gameplay. It turns the complex process of mission development into an experience where users can make decisions and see their consequences.

During development, our team considered scientific and engineering concepts, spacecraft mass and power limits, mission budgets, launch capabilities, orbital selection, communication requirements, scientific instrument choices, and mission reliability. We also considered usability, accessibility, and making the experience understandable for beginners while still offering challenges for more experienced users.

NOVALUX is an educational simulation, not a professional spacecraft engineering or flight-planning tool. Its calculations and mission outcomes are simplified to support learning and experimentation.
